From my agent:

> ### 7. `KeyPackagePublishFailed` used for deletion failures
> 
> `src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs:339` and `:352` — both error sites
> report a *deletion* failure ("could not delete relay event(s)", "left N relay
> event(s) after delete rounds") but wrap it in `WhitenoiseError::KeyPackagePublishFailed`.
> The message text is clear, but the variant misleads anyone matching on error
> types or scanning logs. There is no delete-specific variant today; consider
> adding one, or at least leave a comment noting the deliberate reuse.
>

From my agent:

> ### 6. `mark_completed` upsert writes a column nobody reads
> 
> `src/whitenoise/database/account/maintenance_tasks.rs:41-57` — `mark_completed`
> uses `ON CONFLICT(name) DO UPDATE SET completed_at = excluded.completed_at`, and
> `is_completed` only checks row existence (`SELECT EXISTS`). Nothing in the
> codebase ever reads `completed_at`. So the `DO UPDATE` is dead logic and, worse,
> it overwrites the original completion time with the *last retry* time — the less
> useful value.
> 
> If `completed_at` is kept for debugging/observability, use
> `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` so it records *first* completion. If it is truly
> unused, `INSERT OR IGNORE` (or drop the column) is simpler. Storing a timestamp
> no reader consumes is speculative — prefer the simpler form.

From my agent:

> ### 3. Cleanup permanently orphans local MLS key material for stale key packages
> 
> `src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs:269-396` — the job deletes relay events
> with `delete_mls_stored_keys = false` and never touches the
> `published_key_packages` DB rows. The doc comment at lines 271-274 correctly
> justifies keeping local material (a not-yet-processed Welcome may still need
> it), but it does not acknowledge the consequence: for genuinely stale key
> packages that were *never consumed and never will be* (their relay event is now
> gone, so no new inviter can reach them), the local MLS material and the DB row
> leak forever. `find_eligible_for_cleanup` only reclaims **consumed** packages,
> so nothing ever collects these.
> 
> The leak is small and bounded (one-time, proportional to how many extra key
> packages the account accumulated), so this is not a blocker — but it should be
> a *deliberate* decision. Either extend the doc comment to state the leak is
> accepted, or file a follow-up to reclaim the orphans. Silent leaks age badly.

From my agent:

> ### 2. Delete-then-publish leaves a window with zero key packages on relays
> 
> `src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs:321-364` — the job deletes every
> relay-side key package event, runs the post-delete emptiness check, sleeps
> 500 ms, and only then publishes the fresh pair. For the several seconds this
> spans, the account has **no** key package on any relay, so any peer trying to
> invite it to a group during that window fails to find one.
> 
> The 30 s invite grace and the consumed-key-package deferral reduce the odds,
> but the window is real and re-opens on every thrash from #1.
> 
> Consider inverting the order: publish the fresh pair *first*, then delete every
> key package event *except* the two just-published IDs. The account is never
> without a key package. This is more code (you must thread the new event IDs
> into the delete filter, and the NIP-33 d-tag reuse already replaces the
> same-slot canonical for free), so weigh it against the fact that this is a
> one-time job behind a 30 s grace. But for a security messenger, "briefly
> un-invitable" is worth a deliberate decision rather than an accident of
> ordering.

From my agent:


> ### 1. Strict final verification can cause permanent delete/republish thrash
> 
> `src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs:371-385` — after publishing the fresh
> pair, the job sleeps 500 ms and then requires `has_exact_key_package_pair`:
> *exactly* one canonical, one legacy, total 2. If that check fails the job
> returns `Err`, `mark_completed` is never called, and the next foreground/startup
> re-runs the **whole** cleanup — deleting the pair it just published and
> republishing.
> 
> The verification fetch only sees *reachable* relays (`fetch_all_from_reachable_cleanup_relays`),
> and 500 ms is optimistic for relay round-trip + indexing on a slow or
> eventually-consistent relay. Two realistic ways this thrashes forever:
> 
> - The new pair simply isn't visible within 500 ms → `total != 2` → fail.
> - A relay that was unreachable during the delete phase (so its stale events
>   weren't seen by the post-delete `remaining` check at line 348-357) becomes
>   reachable during verification → `total > 2` → fail forever.
> 
> Every thrash also re-opens the zero-key-package window (see #2). The asymmetry
> matters: a false *failure* costs a permanent delete/republish loop across app
> sessions; a false *success* only leaves the account with extra key packages —
> the benign condition this job exists to clean up.
> 
> Suggestion: have `publish_pair` return the two `EventId`s it published, and make
> verification assert *those two are present* rather than *nothing else exists*.
> That is the invariant you actually care about and it cannot be tripped by relay
> lag or a resurfacing stale relay. Alternatively, downgrade a verification
> mismatch from `Err` to a `warn!` and still `mark_completed`, since delete and
> publish both already succeeded by that point.

`@erskingardner` — thorough and well-structured PR. The double-checked locking, idempotent upsert, and shutdown-aware retry loop are all solid. A few things worth discussing before merging:

---

## Review of PR `#845` — One-time key package relay cleanup

### :warning: Medium — Final `has_recent_consumed_key_package` check after relay cleanup risks repeated MLS key material creation

In `cleanup_relay_key_packages_once`, there is a post-publish check _after_ all the heavy work is done:

```rust
// In src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs

// ... delete loop runs ...
// ... publish_pair() is called, MLS key material is generated ...
// ... verification delay and has_exact_key_package_pair() pass ...

if self.has_recent_consumed_key_package().await? {
    return Ok(KeyPackageRelayCleanupOutcome::DeferredRecentConsumedKeyPackage);  // ← mark_completed NOT called
}
self.session.repos.maintenance_tasks.mark_completed(KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_TASK).await?;
```

If `has_recent_consumed_key_package` returns `true` here (e.g. a Welcome arrived during the 500 ms verify delay), the relay is already in a clean state (exactly one canonical + one legacy event), but `mark_completed` is never called. On the next attempt the entire purge-and-republish cycle repeats, consuming fresh MLS key material unnecessarily. With `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`, this could happen up to three times per app launch.

The intent of the final check appears to be a TOCTOU guard — ensuring no Welcome slipped through just before marking done. But by this point the relay side _is_ clean. Consider either:
- Moving the `mark_completed` call before this last guard (relay cleanup is the goal; the consumed check is only a gate on _starting_ the cleanup), or
- Adding a separate "relay is clean" flag so a subsequent retry can skip the delete loop but still apply the final consumption check before marking complete.

---

### :warning: Medium — Error message in delete loop conflates two different counts

```rust
// In cleanup_relay_key_packages_once
let batch_size = key_package_events.len();  // fetched at round start
let deleted = self.delete_batch_from_relay_urls(...).await?;
total_deleted += deleted;
if deleted == 0 {
    let remaining = self.fetch_all_from_reachable_cleanup_relays(&cleanup_relay_urls).await?;
    return Err(WhitenoiseError::KeyPackagePublishFailed(format!(
        "one-time key package cleanup could not delete {} remaining relay event(s) \
         after round {} found {} event(s)",
        remaining.len(),   // ← post-attempted-deletion count
        round + 1,
        batch_size         // ← pre-deletion count from this same round
    )));
}
```

`remaining.len()` is fetched again after the failed deletion, while `batch_size` was from the fetch at the start of the same round. Between those two points relay state could change (e.g. another client deleted one of the events). This makes the message potentially contradictory (`"could not delete 3 remaining ... after round 1 found 5 events"` where the 3 and 5 weren't observed atomically). A single `remaining` fetch is sufficient for the error message:

```rust
if deleted == 0 {
    let remaining = self.fetch_all_from_reachable_cleanup_relays(&cleanup_relay_urls).await?;
    return Err(WhitenoiseError::KeyPackagePublishFailed(format!(
        "one-time key package cleanup could not delete relay event(s): \
         {} still present after {} deletion attempt(s) in round {}",
        remaining.len(),
        max_retries + 1,
        round + 1,
    )));
}
```

---

### :information_source: Low — `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS` serves two semantically different roles

```rust
// Used as the foreground delay:
const KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(
    crate::whitenoise::session::key_packages::KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS,
);

// Also used as the has_consumed_since quiet period:
self.session.repos.published_key_packages
    .has_consumed_since(KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS as i64)
```

"How long to wait after app foreground before running cleanup" and "how recently a key package was consumed" are logically distinct policy values. They happen to be equal (30 s) now, but naming the shared constant `_INVITE_GRACE_SECS` and using it in both places means a future change to one will silently affect the other. Consider extracting:

```rust
pub(crate) const KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS: u64 = 30;
pub(crate) const KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_QUIET_PERIOD_SECS: u64 = KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS; // intentionally equal for now
```

---

### :information_source: Nit — `fetch_all_from_reachable_cleanup_relays` is a transparent wrapper

```rust
async fn fetch_all_from_reachable_cleanup_relays(&self, relay_urls: &[RelayUrl]) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {
    // Keep this as one multi-relay request so the ephemeral relay plane can
    // use its existing partial-connect behavior. ...
    self.fetch_all_from_relay_urls(relay_urls).await
}
```

The comment references "partial-connect behavior" as the reason for this wrapper, but the wrapper adds no logic beyond forwarding the call. Either the partial-connect handling is already transparently inside `fetch_all_from_relay_urls` (in which case the comment is accurate but the wrapper buys nothing) or it's aspirational. If the former, the wrapper is redundant; if the latter, the comment is slightly misleading. Either way, a sentence clarifying which applies would help readers.

---

### :information_source: Nit — Inline table creation in tests bypasses schema validation

Both `maintenance_tasks.rs` and the account-level `published_key_packages.rs` test setups manually drop and recreate tables rather than running the migration:

```rust
// src/whitenoise/database/account/maintenance_tasks.rs (test setup)
sqlx::query("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS account_maintenance_tasks").execute(...).await.unwrap();
sqlx::query("CREATE TABLE account_maintenance_tasks (...)").execute(...).await.unwrap();
```

The code itself has a comment warning about this:
> `// NOTE: the CREATE TABLE below must stay in sync with fresh_account_schema.sql`

The `m0046_account_maintenance_tasks.rs` tests do properly exercise the migrator. The inline patterns in the other files are an existing project-wide pattern; the `setup_account_db_with_migrations` helper called out in the comment would be the right long-term fix to prevent schema drift from going undetected in unit tests.

---

### :white_check_mark: What looks solid

- **Migration correctness**: `m0046` uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` inside a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction with idempotency validated by the migration runner's `_rust_migrations` tracking.
- **`mark_completed` upsert**: the `ON CONFLICT(name) DO UPDATE SET completed_at = excluded.completed_at` ensures retries are safe.
- **Double-checked locking**: the post-lock re-check of both `is_completed` and `has_recent_consumed_key_package` correctly guards against concurrent Welcome processing.
- **`has_exact_key_package_pair` total-count check**: `events.len() == 2` prevents false positives from mixed results where canonical + legacy counts happen to equal 1 each but there are additional unknown-kind events.
- **Shutdown-aware retry loop**: the `tokio::select!` over both `sleep` and `shutdown_rx.changed()` is well-formed.
- **Test coverage**: shutdown-already-started, grace-period wait, shutdown-during-delay, and the schedule→complete lifecycle are all exercised independently.
- **`backdate_consumed_at` in tests**: keeps canonical/legacy twins in sync (via `key_package_hash_ref` scoping) so `find_eligible_for_cleanup`'s `NOT EXISTS` sub-clause doesn't falsely trip.

**Claude finished @erskingardner's task in 2m 49s** —— [View job](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/actions/runs/26180761604)

---
### Code Review

- [x] Gather context and understand the request
- [x] Read changed files
- [x] Review database/migration layer
- [x] Review key package cleanup logic
- [x] Review foreground catchup integration

---

Overall this is solid work. The architecture is clean — double-checked locking, idempotent task markers, good unit test coverage. Both issues CodeRabbit flagged (missing pre-sleep shutdown check, `DeferredRecentConsumedKeyPackage` return after delete phase) are properly addressed in the latest commit.

A few things worth flagging:

---

### Medium: Unnecessary post-verify deferred return

**`src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs`, lines 385–387**

```rust
if self.has_recent_consumed_key_package().await? {
    return Ok(KeyPackageRelayCleanupOutcome::DeferredRecentConsumedKeyPackage);
}
```

This check fires *after* the delete loop completed and `has_exact_key_package_pair` verified the relay state is clean (exactly one canonical + one legacy pair). At that point the task has succeeded — returning `Deferred` instead of marking it complete causes the full delete+publish cycle to run again on the next retry attempt.

If a Welcome arrived mid-cleanup (between delete rounds), the post-republish verification at line 372 already caught any issues — a mismatched pair count would have returned an error there. A recently consumed key package at this stage doesn't affect whether our published pair is correct. Dropping this check and going straight to `mark_completed` would be semantically cleaner. At minimum, a comment explaining *why* we defer even after a successful verification would help future readers.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fwhitenoise%2Fsession%2Fkey_packages.rs%20around%20line%20385%2C%20the%20post-verify%20has_recent_consumed_key_package%20check%20in%20cleanup_relay_key_packages_once%20returns%20DeferredRecentConsumedKeyPackage%20after%20has_exact_key_package_pair%20already%20verified%20the%20relay%20state%20is%20clean.%20This%20causes%20unnecessary%20repeat%20delete%2Bpublish%20cycles.%20Consider%20removing%20this%20post-verify%20deferred%20check%20and%20going%20directly%20to%20mark_completed%2C%20or%20add%20a%20comment%20explaining%20the%20rationale%20for%20deferring%20even%20after%20successful%20verification.%20Branch%3A%20codex%2Fkey-package-relay-cleanup&repo=marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs)

---

### Low: One constant doing two jobs

`KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS` (30 s) is used as both the foreground cleanup delay and the `has_consumed_since` quiet period window. These are currently the same value but have different semantics:

- **Delay**: how long to wait after foreground resume before attempting cleanup  
- **Quiet period**: how recent a consumed key package needs to be to block cleanup  

If either value needs to change independently (e.g. bump the quiet period to 60 s without changing the startup delay), both concepts need to be untangled. Consider naming them separately — `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_DELAY_SECS` vs `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_QUIET_PERIOD_SECS`.

---

### Low: Alphabetical sort in `merge_cleanup_relay_urls` drops priority order

**`src/whitenoise/session/key_packages.rs`, line 981**

```rust
relay_urls.sort_unstable_by(|left, right| left.as_str().cmp(right.as_str()));
```

The deduplication logic inserts key-package relays first, then NIP-65, then defaults — encoding a priority preference. The alphabetical sort silently discards that order. For cleanup this is harmless since all relays are used regardless, but the sort is unnecessary and could confuse someone who adds priority-sensitive logic later. If deterministic ordering is needed for testability, that's worth calling out in a comment. Otherwise removing the sort or sorting only for test stability makes the intent clearer.

---

### Low: Test schema drift warning is missing in `maintenance_tasks.rs`

`src/whitenoise/database/account/maintenance_tasks.rs` test `setup()` drops and recreates the `account_maintenance_tasks` table directly (lines 72–84). The adjacent `published_key_packages.rs` has an explicit comment warning that "the CREATE TABLE below must stay in sync with `fresh_account_schema.sql`". The same caveat belongs in the `maintenance_tasks.rs` test setup since the same drift risk applies.

---

### Info: 3-attempt retry cap is bounded but silent on persistent defer

In `foreground_catchup.rs` the retry loop runs at most `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` times, with `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_DELAY` (= `KEY_PACKAGE_RELAY_CLEANUP_INVITE_GRACE_SECS` = 30 s in prod) between attempts. That means if welcomes arrive continuously for ~90+ seconds after startup, cleanup logs a `warn!` and gives up. The task remains unmarked, so it will retry the next time the foreground path fires (next app resume). This seems like the correct safety valve — just confirming it's intentional design rather than an oversight.

---

### Positive callouts

- The double-checked `is_completed` + `has_recent_consumed_key_package` pattern before and after acquiring `_publish_guard` is exactly right for preventing TOCTOU races with concurrent Welcome-triggered rotations.
- `MaintenanceTasksRepo::mark_completed` using `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` is a clean idempotent upsert — safe to retry without duplicate rows.
- The `relay_cleanup_policy_constants_are_stable` test that pins the string key and numeric constants is a nice touch to prevent accidental renames invalidating stored task markers.
- Shutdown check before the grace period sleep (`*shutdown_rx.borrow()` early return) correctly addresses the Tokio `watch` receiver semantics where pre-subscription state changes are considered "seen".

issue.body:
White Noise community signal data

116 touchpoints in 6 months. 58 GitHub issues. 58 community chat messages. All three of the same topics.

I appreciate that the team is spending real time answering the same questions while simultaneously trying to build. This report breaks down what those questions are, what the answers are, and exactly where to put them so the team stops being the first line of support.

Part 1: top 3 issues by volume (last 6 months)

Issue | GitHub issues | Chat messages | Total -- | -- | -- | -- Can't add someone to a group / keypackage errors | 23 (10 open, 13 closed) | ~28 messages | ~51 Messages and notifications not getting through | 21 (7 open, 14 closed) | ~18 messages | ~39 What files can I send / what are the size limits | 14 (6 open, 8 closed) | ~12 messages | ~26

Part 2: canned responses

1. Can't add someone to a group / getting an error when inviting someone

Thanks for flagging this. While we work on a permanent fix, here's what resolves it in most cases.

Go to Developer Settings and find Keypackage Management. You should have two keypackages, not more. If you have more than two, tap Delete Legacy to clean them up, then try the invite again.

Overall this is a clean, well-structured addition. The doc comments are thorough, the failure-tolerance model is clearly reasoned, and the test coverage covers the important cases. I have one moderate concern and a couple of minor nits.

### Moderate: Message replay can overflow the broadcast buffer

`FOREGROUND_MESSAGE_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT` is 200, but `BroadcastHub`'s `BUFFER_SIZE` is 100. The replay loop in `replay_message_stream_snapshot_for_group` ([`foreground_catchup.rs:191-199`](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs/blob/codex/add-foreground-resume-catchup/src/whitenoise/foreground_catchup.rs#L191-L199)) fires up to 200 `send()` calls into a channel buffered for 100. Tokio's broadcast channel silently drops the oldest messages on overflow and marks receivers `Lagged`. A Flutter consumer that was suspended in the background (the exact scenario this method targets) will not be draining the channel while the replay is running. If the snapshot for an open group has more than 100 messages, the consumer will receive a `Lagged` error rather than the full snapshot.

The simplest fix is to either lower `FOREGROUND_MESSAGE_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT` to ≤ `BUFFER_SIZE`, raise `BUFFER_SIZE`, or emit a single batched update type instead of individual per-message sends. The comment in the doc already tells callers to use `fetch_aggregated_messages_for_group` for exact replacement, so capping the replay limit to 100 (or even 50) would also be consistent with that guidance.

### Minor: `update_trigger_debug_output` test doesn't cover `SnapshotRefresh`

`chat_list_streaming/types.rs:96-126` tests all `ChatListUpdateTrigger` variants in `Debug` output but stops before `SnapshotRefresh`. The serialization roundtrip test at line 84 does include it, so this is purely cosmetic, but it's inconsistent.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fwhitenoise%2Fchat_list_streaming%2Ftypes.rs%20on%20branch%20codex%2Fadd-foreground-resume-catchup%2C%20the%20update_trigger_debug_output%20test%20(lines%2096-126)%20tests%20all%20ChatListUpdateTrigger%20variants%20except%20SnapshotRefresh.%20Add%20a%20debug%20assertion%20for%20ChatListUpdateTrigger%3A%3ASnapshotRefresh%20to%20match%20the%20other%20variants.&repo=marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs)

issue.title: Per-account gift-wrap decrypt throttle with deferral semantics
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-account token bucket gating NIP-44 decryption of inbound gift-wrap (`kind:1059`) events, with three-way result classification so each event class has the right outcome.

## Motivation

Inbound `kind:1059` events have no sender authentication discoverable before NIP-44 decryption — the recipient must perform secp256k1 ECDH and AEAD decrypt on every event addressed to them, and the KeyPackage reference that would identify the inviter sits inside the encrypted rumor. Without a budget, anyone who knows a recipient's pubkey can force unbounded per-event ECDH work on the recipient's device.

This change bounds that work at the client without changing the protocol.

## What changed

**Throttle.** `GiftwrapThrottle` is a per-account token bucket on `AccountSession` (capacity 60, refill 2/sec). Acquired immediately before `extract_rumor` and after the signer-availability check, so unavailable signers don't drain the budget.

**Single decrypt per event.** Sync-watermark advancement (`update_last_synced_max`) is now done inside `handle_giftwrap` using the rumor timestamp returned by the same `extract_rumor` call, removing the previous post-success second decrypt of the same event.

**Three-way outcome classification.** `extract_rumor` failures are mapped at the source:

| Class | Detection | Outer outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Throttled | bucket empty | `Err(GiftwrapThrottled)` → no track, no retry (relay replay redelivers after refill) |
| External-signer decrypt failed | `nip59::Error::Signer` with non-`Keys` backend | `Err(GiftwrapDeferred)` → no track, no retry (relay replay redelivers after signer recovers) |
| Terminal (malformed payload / local Keys decrypt failed) | any other `Err` | `Ok(())` + warn log → tracked, deduped against future redelivery |
| Success | — | `Ok(())` → tracked, watermark advanced |

The deferral cases deliberately avoid the in-process retry queue, which would re-acquire a token on each of up to 10 retries (`RetryInfo::max_attempts`).

## Tests

Five new unit tests in `giftwrap_throttle::tests` cover the bucket math (trickle, flood, refill cap, sustained-flood throughput, mutex-poison fail-open). Three new integration tests in `account_event_processor::tests` pin the contracts at the boundary:

- `test_throttled_giftwrap_is_not_recorded_as_processed` — exhausts the bucket, sends a valid `kind:1059`, asserts the event is NOT in `already_processed_account_event`.
- `test_undecryptable_giftwrap_is_terminal_not_retried` — sends garbage ciphertext with a local Keys signer, asserts the event IS marked processed AND exactly one token (not eleven) was consumed.
- `test_external_signer_decrypt_failure_is_deferred_not_terminal` — installs a `FailingExternalSigner` (`SignerBackend::Custom`, every `nip44_decrypt` fails), asserts the event is NOT marked processed AND exactly one token was consumed.

## Test plan

- [x] `just precommit-quick` green locally (verified)
- [ ] Manual sanity on physical device after merge: confirm no regression in normal welcome flow.

issue.title: Per-account gift-wrap decrypt throttle with deferral semantics
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds a per-account token bucket gating NIP-44 decryption of inbound gift-wrap (`kind:1059`) events, with three-way result classification so each event class has the right outcome.

## Motivation

Inbound `kind:1059` events have no sender authentication discoverable before NIP-44 decryption — the recipient must perform secp256k1 ECDH and AEAD decrypt on every event addressed to them, and the KeyPackage reference that would identify the inviter sits inside the encrypted rumor. Without a budget, anyone who knows a recipient's pubkey can force unbounded per-event ECDH work on the recipient's device.

This change bounds that work at the client without changing the protocol.

## What changed

**Throttle.** `GiftwrapThrottle` is a per-account token bucket on `AccountSession` (capacity 60, refill 2/sec). Acquired immediately before `extract_rumor` and after the signer-availability check, so unavailable signers don't drain the budget.

**Single decrypt per event.** Sync-watermark advancement (`update_last_synced_max`) is now done inside `handle_giftwrap` using the rumor timestamp returned by the same `extract_rumor` call, removing the previous post-success second decrypt of the same event.

**Three-way outcome classification.** `extract_rumor` failures are mapped at the source:

| Class | Detection | Outer outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Throttled | bucket empty | `Err(GiftwrapThrottled)` → no track, no retry (relay replay redelivers after refill) |
| External-signer decrypt failed | `nip59::Error::Signer` with non-`Keys` backend | `Err(GiftwrapDeferred)` → no track, no retry (relay replay redelivers after signer recovers) |
| Terminal (malformed payload / local Keys decrypt failed) | any other `Err` | `Ok(())` + warn log → tracked, deduped against future redelivery |
| Success | — | `Ok(())` → tracked, watermark advanced |

The deferral cases deliberately avoid the in-process retry queue, which would re-acquire a token on each of up to 10 retries (`RetryInfo::max_attempts`).

## Tests

Five new unit tests in `giftwrap_throttle::tests` cover the bucket math (trickle, flood, refill cap, sustained-flood throughput, mutex-poison fail-open). Three new integration tests in `account_event_processor::tests` pin the contracts at the boundary:

- `test_throttled_giftwrap_is_not_recorded_as_processed` — exhausts the bucket, sends a valid `kind:1059`, asserts the event is NOT in `already_processed_account_event`.
- `test_undecryptable_giftwrap_is_terminal_not_retried` — sends garbage ciphertext with a local Keys signer, asserts the event IS marked processed AND exactly one token (not eleven) was consumed.
- `test_external_signer_decrypt_failure_is_deferred_not_terminal` — installs a `FailingExternalSigner` (`SignerBackend::Custom`, every `nip44_decrypt` fails), asserts the event is NOT marked processed AND exactly one token was consumed.

## Test plan

- [x] `just precommit-quick` green locally (verified)
- [ ] Manual sanity on physical device after merge: confirm no regression in normal welcome flow.
